Fed's Collins says another cut is possible if job growth keeps slowing

By Ann Kowalski October 26, 2026 1:12 PM UTC

BOSTON, Oct 26 (Wire Desk) - Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said on Monday the U.S. central bank could lower interest rates again in December if hiring continues to cool, though she wants to see more data before deciding.

"I'm open to a further reduction this year, but it is not a done deal," Collins said in remarks prepared for a conference in Boston. "Inflation is still running above our 2% goal."

The Fed cut its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point last month to the 3.75%-4.00% range, its second reduction this year. Futures markets on Monday priced a roughly 68% chance of another quarter-point cut at the Dec. 9-10 meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

U.S. employers added 61,000 jobs in September, fewer than the 110,000 economists had expected, and the unemployment rate edged up to 4.4%, the highest in four years.

Core personal consumption expenditures inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.8% in the 12 months through August. Collins said she expects it to fall toward 2.5% by the end of next year as the effect of tariffs fades.

Collins, who is not a voter on the rate-setting committee this year, said the labor market was "in a low-hire, low-fire state" that could turn quickly. She said the balance of risks had shifted toward weaker employment since the summer.

Treasury yields were little changed after her remarks, with the two-year note at 3.52%. The dollar index slipped 0.2%.

Reporting by Ann Kowalski; Editing by Paul Brenner
